comments.body: `access_token_expires_at` and `refresh_token_expires_at` are computed as `Date.now() + response.expires_in * 1000` and `Date.now() + response.refresh_token_expires_in * 1000`, then `.toISOString()` is called on each. GitHub only returns `expires_in` and `refresh_token_expires_in` when token expiration is enabled. For OAuth Apps, and for GitHub Apps with expiring user tokens turned off, both fields are missing. Then `undefined * 1000` is NaN, `new Date(NaN).toISOString()` throws `RangeError: Invalid time value`, and the surrounding catch returns `{success:false, error:'Invalid time value'}`. Login always fails for those apps even when the code exchange succeeded. Guard each expiry field and only compute it when the value is present.

The token exchange URL is built by string interpolation, and `code` comes from `req.query.code ?? req.body.code` without `encodeURIComponent`. `clientId` and `clientSecret` are not encoded either. A caller can send `code=x&redirect_uri=...` and inject or override parameters in the request to github.com that carries the client secret. An array or object `code` is also stringified. Use `URLSearchParams` or encode every value. Separately, GitHub answers a bad or expired code with HTTP 200 and `{error, error_description}`. That case reaches `upsert_`, which returns 'No access token found'. `validateCallback` drops the `error` field (line 763), so the route reports only the generic 'Authentication failed'.

For OAuth providers, `GET /auth/:actor/:provider` used to answer with `res.redirect(location)`. It now returns a 200 JSON body `{ location }`. A browser navigating or linking to this endpoint, which was the documented Google flow, no longer redirects and just shows JSON. Only callers that use `sdk.auth.login` (POST) and handle `location` keep working. The PR description lists three breaking changes and this one is not among them.
